label: The repo plugin fleet consumes v1 hooks-bag events (event: async ({event}) with event.type/event.properties); v2 has no hooks bag and instead exposes ctx.event.subscribe({signal}) as an async iterable yielding {type,data}, plus ctx.session.hook('prompt') for prompt delivery, so every fleet plugin needs a transport adapter and version detection must be a feature probe on the context

session.idle and session.compacted are the fleet's two load-bearing events with no v2 peer: the reference v2 translator has no session.idle input and synthesizes idle as session.status{type:'idle'} from session.execution.succeeded|failed|interrupted, while session.compacted has no substitute at all, leaving system-completion-sentinel (idle-sole-trigger), system-skill-advisor and system-spec-gate (compaction re-arm) without triggers on v2

Event payload field names are renamed between versions: v2 permission.asked carries action/resources where the fleet reads permission/patterns, and v2 replaces question.asked|replied|rejected with form.created|replied|cancelled carrying a nested form{fields[],sessionID,id} that must be rebuilt into question option shape with id to requestID

v2's own event vocabulary is not stable: the same reference plugin carries two normalizers for two v2-era schemes (session.next.step.started|tool.called|tool.progress|retried, permission.v2.*, question.v2.* versus session.execution.*, session.text.*, form.*), so a port must normalize event families rather than pin one naming scheme

A single plugin module can host both contracts through a load-time selector on the default export (OpenCode 1 needs a callable default, OpenCode 2 validates an object), with a server field on the v2 object embedding the v1 hooks factory, so a two-file split is optional; the observed selector is an environment variable, which a repo-installed plugin cannot rely on

v2 documents plugin discovery as package-shaped per-plugin directories (<project>/.opencode/plugins/<name>/index.ts plus tui.ts, and <global-config>/plugins/<name>/index.ts plus tui.ts) while the repo ships 16 flat .js files under .opencode/plugins/ including one symlinked module, so flat-file loading on v2 is unverified and the port may be a layout migration before any code change

TUI output is fully available on v2 through @opencode/plugin/tui and context.ui.toast.show({message,variant}), with data.on/data.listen for server events, attention.notify, dialogs, keymap layers and storage, but no repo plugin renders UI at all (zero hits for showToast, client.tui, toast and tui. across .skilled/plugins), so toast capability does not gate the fleet port

TUI plugin registration config diverges per version: v1 uses tui.json with the singular plugin key holding file:// entries, v2 uses cli.json with the plural plugins key accepting package ids, pkg@version, relative and absolute paths, file:// URLs, object {package,options} form and dash-prefixed disable patterns, and neither host is documented to read the other's file or key, so a dual install must ship both

cli-opencode documents the run --format json stream as session.started/message.delta/tool.call/tool.result/session.completed with a session_id, and nothing in the repo parses those names; the repo's own captured v1 stream instead emits {type,timestamp,sessionID,id,messageID,part} records with part.state.{status,input,output,metadata,title}, so the documented schema is likely fabricated and the cli-opencode v2 flag matrix cannot be written from it

opencode run --help and opencode2 run --help are both refused in this session by the local dispatch guard, so no flag diff and no real run --format json capture was possible although both binaries are installed (1.19.3 and 2.0.32)
A dual-version plugin cannot pin a v2 event name: at least two v2-era vocabularies coexist, so the only stable contract is a normalizer plus a feature probe on the context

Version detection must not depend on a version string: the reference plugin probes typeof ctx.session.hook and typeof ctx.event.subscribe, which is the only host-derived signal observed on a working dual install
